part.name: Pedestal-mounted C-frame bracket with threaded top boss
part.description: Single-piece mechanical bracket comprising an elongated two-hole mounting flange, a thick asymmetric C-shaped load frame, a central fork/guide structure, opposed capsule-shaped side recesses, and an upper threaded cylindrical interface. STEP envelope is 168 mm x 180 mm x 60 mm with 67 B-rep faces.
part.symmetry_note: The mounting flange, top boss, transverse head hole, and capsule recesses are approximately symmetric about the mid-depth plane z=-21 mm. The part is not symmetric along its length because of the asymmetric C-frame and internal fork geometry.

Section.name: Mounting base flange
Section.function intent: Provides the primary fixed interface to a machine bed, plate, or fixture and establishes the bracket's datum plane.
Section.physical behavior: The broad lower face reacts compression and overturning moment, while the two spaced through holes accept fasteners and resist sliding and rotation. Rounded corners reduce edge stress and handling hazards.
Section.geometry: A long rectangular flange spanning the full part width, with four rounded plan-view corners and two widely spaced cylindrical through holes. The flange is approximately 15 mm thick and extends beyond both sides of the upright structure.
Section.location: Bottom of the part, extending laterally to both ends beneath the C-frame.

major_faces.description: Cylindrical wall of the mounting hole near the x=153 mm end of the flange.

major_faces.name: Base top seating face
major_faces.description: Large horizontal upper surface of the flange surrounding the upright and both mounting holes.

major_faces.name: Left mounting-hole wall
major_faces.description: Cylindrical wall of the mounting hole near the x=15 mm end of the flange.

major_faces.name: Base bottom mounting face
major_faces.description: Large flat underside that seats against the supporting machine or fixture.

major_faces.name: Long outer flange edge
major_faces.description: Long vertical edge face along the z=-60 mm side of the mounting flange.

Section.name: Primary C-frame
Section.function intent: Forms the main load path between the top interface and mounting flange while leaving a large side-access opening for a mating component or workpiece.
Section.physical behavior: The thick front and rear webs act as bending plates, while the curved outer spine carries tension and compression around the throat. The generous curved perimeter distributes stress and reduces concentration at the transition from the head to the lower upright.
Section.geometry: A depth-extruded asymmetric C-shaped frame with broad planar front and back faces. It includes a tall rectangular upper head, a curved descending spine, a lower vertical leg, and a large irregular throat opening.
Section.location: Rises from the mounting flange through the center-right of the part and continues to the upper head.

major_faces.description: Large planar z=-42 mm face defining the rear profile of the main C-frame.

Section.name: Internal fork and guide structure
Section.function intent: Provides an internal locating, guiding, or reaction feature inside the C-frame opening while maintaining clearance around a mating element.
Section.physical behavior: The stepped rib locally stiffens the lower frame and can react contact loads from a mating part. Its inclined and curved surfaces guide insertion and transfer localized force into the surrounding front and back webs.
Section.geometry: A narrower internal fork-like structure occupying the C-frame throat. It has planar faces at intermediate depth levels z=-12 mm and z=-30 mm, vertical side walls, an inclined facet, and small cylindrical transitions.
Section.location: Inside the lower-left portion of the C-shaped opening, between the front and rear structural webs.

major_faces.description: Rear counterpart of the lower fork ledge, located at z=-30 mm.

Section.name: Opposed capsule recesses
Section.function intent: Provides localized clearance, weight reduction, tool access, or travel space on both depth sides of the lower upright.
Section.physical behavior: The recessed floors reduce local wall thickness without fully penetrating the frame. Rounded ends avoid the high stress concentration that would occur at sharp-ended slots and preserve load flow around the pockets.
Section.geometry: Two opposed blind obround pockets centered near x=113 mm and y=55 mm. Each pocket has a flat floor, two straight vertical side walls, and upper and lower semicylindrical end walls; the front pocket spans z=0 to -10 mm and the rear spans z=-32 to -42 mm.
Section.location: On the front and back sides of the lower right upright, below the curved spine.

Section.name: Upper interface head and threaded boss
Section.function intent: Provides a coaxial threaded mounting interface for an actuator, adjustment screw, sensor, or fitting, while the transverse hole offers secondary retention, cross-pinning, lubrication, or access.
Section.physical behavior: The cylindrical boss locates the mating component radially and its internal thread carries axial load and torque. The annular shoulder reacts seating compression, while toroidal and spline blends spread boss loads into the rectangular head. The transverse hole can accept a pin or provide access through the head.
Section.geometry: A rectangular head terminates in a planar top platform carrying a centered vertical cylindrical boss. The boss has a chamfered top rim, an annular top face, an axial bore aligned with the y-axis, and blended lower shoulders. A small radius-3 mm transverse hole crosses the head along the x-axis.
Section.location: Top of the part, centered over the upper rectangular head.
